notation.meaning: Second derivative: change in the slope in direction $i$ as $x_j$ changes
Small step away from a point
Point the approximation is built around

blocks.md: The Hessian collects all the second derivatives of a function into a table: how fast each slope is itself changing, in every direction and combination of directions. It describes the curvature of the surface. At a flat spot, curvature tells you what you are standing on — the bottom of a bowl, the top of a dome, or a saddle that curves up one way and down another. Its off-diagonal entries say whether two inputs reinforce each other.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It is the tool for checking that a solution is really a maximum or minimum, and for measuring complementarity between inputs.

blocks.tex: H(\mathbf{x}) = \begin{pmatrix} f_{11} & f_{12} & \cdots\\ f_{21} & f_{22} & \cdots\\ \vdots & & \ddots\end{pmatrix}, \qquad f_{ij} = \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i\,\partial x_j}

blocks.md: **Young's theorem**: if the second partials are continuous, $f_{ij} = f_{ji}$, so $H$ is symmetric.
At a critical point ($\nabla f = \mathbf{0}$), the second-order Taylor term $\tfrac12\mathbf{d}'H\mathbf{d}$ decides the shape ([Taylor Series Approximation](note:taylor-series-approximation)):

| $H$ at the critical point | Point is |
| --- | --- |
| Positive definite | Local minimum |
| Negative definite | Local maximum |
| Indefinite | Saddle point |
| Semidefinite | Test inconclusive |
$f(x,y) = x^2 + xy + y^2$: $H = \begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$, eigenvalues 3 and 1 → PD, so $(0,0)$ is a minimum.
$f_{12} > 0$ means the inputs are **complements**: more of one raises the marginal product of the other. In production, skill-capital complementarity is a statement about a cross-partial.

- **Econometrics**: the Hessian of $\mathbf{e}'\mathbf{e}$ is $2\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$, which is PD under full rank — so OLS is a minimum ([OLS in Matrix Form](note:ols-in-matrix-form)); in MLE, the negative inverse Hessian estimates the variance.
- **Optimization**: [Unconstrained Optimization](note:unconstrained-optimization), [Convexity and Concavity](note:convexity-and-concavity).
